patch_description: The original program returned an empty configuration. Instead of copying lattice-based constructions (which create collinear triples with zero area) or pure random search, I use a hybrid: a deterministic, seeded stochastic hill-climb over the 11 point coordinates that directly maximizes the minimum triangle area (computed vectorized over all 165 triplets). Key insights: (1) soft-start from a spread-out interior configuration rather than a lattice to avoid degenerate collinear triples; (2) fold points back into the triangle via barycentric clamping so every perturbation stays feasible; (3) geometric step-size annealing to refine from coarse exploration to fine-tuning. The method is fully deterministic via a fixed seed and runs fast since each evaluation is a vectorized 165-triplet area computation.
